news.title: Samoa suffer record 17-0 defeat to United States at FIFA U-17 World Cup
news.lede: Samoa have suffered a record 17-0 defeat to the United States in their opening Group E match at the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco. The Pacific Islanders were overwhelmed by the Americans, who scored nine goals before half-time and added eight more after the break. The result was the biggest winning margin in FIFA Women’s World Cup history, across all age groups. American forward Maddie DiMaria led the scoring with six goals, setting a tournament record for the most goals scored by an individual player in one match.

news.title: CommBank Junior Matildas draw 1-1 with Chile in historic first FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup™ point
news.lede: The CommBank Junior Matildas have come from behind to draw 1-1 with Chile in their opening game of the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup. Charlotte Bradshaw’s second-half goal earned the side their first-ever point in their first game at the tournament. Head Coach Mike Cooper named an exciting young side for the first game of the tournament. Willa Pearson wore the captain’s armband in the centre of defence, while Leyla Hussein and Kaya Jugovic were up top in a front two.

news.title: Football Ferns book Porirua Park for two-match series against Philippines
news.lede: The Football Ferns will complete their 2026 international programme with two matches against the Philippines at Wellington’s Porirua Park. The games, on Sunday November 29 and Friday December 4, will provide more preparation for next year’s FIFA Women’s World Cup in Brazil. The Philippines are ranked #39 in the FIFA women’s world rankings and will provide opposition for coach Michael Mayne’s side, who are #32. The series follows the cancellation of New Zealand’s planned October internationals against Panama after an earthquake struck the Central American country.

news.title: Infantino set to take his FIFA re-election campaign to Japan to court Asian soccer federations
news.lede: TOKYO (AP) — Gianni Infantino's campaign for re-election as FIFA president is set to move this week to Japan and a meeting scheduled for Wednesday with the Asian Football Confederation. This comes after Infantino apologized last week in Zurich, Switzerland, to FIFA's 37-member ruling council — which he chairs — for “mistakes” he made in assembling a now-scrapped $4.2 billion sell-off plan for the World Cup. The council is the main decision-making body at FIFA with a global spread of officials. The planned meeting with Asian soccer leaders is to be held in a five-star hotel in Tokyo with the media largely excluded.

news.title: CommBank ParaMatildas defeat Netherlands 13-0 to finish IFCPF Women’s World Cup group stage on a high
news.lede: The CommBank ParaMatildas have finished their group stage campaign with a 13-0 victory over the Netherlands. Annmarie de Uriarte added five to her considerable goal-scoring total, while Trinity McPhie scored a hat-trick, Lainee Harrison and Katelyn Smith struck braces, and Leah Spaine put away her fifth of the tournament. The result means that Australia has finished top of Group B and will take on Finland, who finished second in Group A, in the semi-finals. There were three changes to the starting five that defeated Colombia last time out.

news.title: Pearson: We really played like Aussies
news.lede: Australian captain and FIFA Player of the Match, Willa Pearson, praised the Aussie spirit of her team after the CommBank Junior Matildas secured a hard-fought 1-1 draw against Chile in their historic FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup Morocco 2026™ debut. Competing at the tournament for the first time in Australian football history, the CommBank Junior Matildas were forced to come from behind after Chile's Kiara Concha opened the scoring in the 33rd minute. Australia responded in the second half through substitute Charlotte Bradshaw, who converted a Sakura Leong delivery in the 63rd minute to score the nation's first-ever goal at a FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup™. "We talk about Aussie spirit all the time, and that's definitely what we showed today," the Sydney FC defender said.

news.title: Football Ferns to end 2026 with home series against Philippines
news.lede: As the Football Ferns gathered for a team meeting to name the squad to play Panama, they were interrupted by violent shaking. A magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck southern Panama on Friday, damaging homes, cutting power, halting flights and sending residents into the streets, while triggering more than a dozen aftershocks.
